On the other hand, the dominant empirical tradition, following John Locke, holds that the mind is a 'tabula rasa' (blank slate) at birth that all knowledge — including mathematical truths — is acquired solely through sensory experience ; Locke argued that anything else would require reasoning to discover it that it is contradictory to say knowledge exists innately yet remains unknown until reason is applied

Philosophers such as Plato and Descartes had argued earlier that certain knowledge — including mathematical truisms and abstract forms — is inborn and becomes apparent through reflection on one's own nature , while more recent research in cognitive science challenges even this, noting that mathematical perception may itself be an innate capacity to process numbers rather than a purely acquired skill
